questions.q: What is the current, supported name and generation of the Salesforce CLI used throughout this course?
options: sfdx v1, using colon-separated commands like force:org:create
sf (v2), using space-separated commands like sf org create scratch
force-cli, Salesforce's original 2015 tool
salesforce-cli-legacy
questions.explain: The CLI was rebuilt as sf (v2) with space-separated commands and the force topic dropped from most commands; the older sfdx/sf v1 generation with colon-separated force: commands is deprecated.

questions.q: Which npm command installs the current Salesforce CLI?
options: npm install --global @salesforce/cli
npm install --global sfdx-cli
npm install --global force-cli
npm install --global salesforce-dx
questions.explain: The current CLI ships as the npm package @salesforce/cli, installed globally with npm install --global @salesforce/cli.

questions.q: A version string from `sf version` reads `@salesforce/cli/2.65.6 win32-x64 node-v20.11.0`. What does the leading `2` confirm?
options: That exactly 2 plugins are installed
That this is the current sf (v2) generation of the CLI, not the deprecated sf v1 bundled in the old sfdx
That the CLI was installed exactly 2 days ago
That the CLI supports only 2 target orgs at a time
questions.explain: A version string beginning with @salesforce/cli/2 confirms the current sf (v2) CLI generation, distinguishing it from the deprecated sf v1 that shipped bundled with sfdx.

questions.q: Why should you update an npm-installed Salesforce CLI with `npm install --global @salesforce/cli@latest` rather than `sf update`?
options: sf update deletes all authenticated orgs
sf update is reserved for the standalone installer's own auto-update mechanism and doesn't work for npm installs
There is no difference; both commands are identical
sf update only works on macOS
questions.explain: sf update is the standalone installer's auto-update path; for an npm install, the CLI itself will tell you to update via npm install --global @salesforce/cli@latest instead.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against installing the Salesforce CLI via both the standalone installer AND npm on the same machine?
options: It's actually recommended, for redundancy
Doing both causes path conflicts between the two installations that are difficult to debug
Only one installation method is legally licensed per machine
npm installs are always slower than standalone installers
questions.explain: Installing via both methods causes conflicting entries in your system PATH pointing at two different CLI installations, which is a genuinely confusing problem to diagnose — pick one method and stick with it.
